newsitem.title: USA: U.S. meat/poultry exports up 9.4 pct in '96 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. meat/poultry exports up 9.4 pct in '96 - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said total U.S. meat and poultry exports rose 9.4 percent to $6.5 billion in 1996 from $5.9 billion in 1995, fuelled by strong pork and poultry exports.
In its monthly U.S. Agricultural Trade Update, USDA's Economic Research Service said pork exports increased 19 percent in 1996 to $940 million and were nearly double the 1994 level of $499 million.
Poultry meat exports grew almost 26 percent in 1996, reaching a year-to-date total of $2.3 billion and surpassing beef and veal exports, USDA said.
It said poultry meat exports to the former Soviet Union were up 67 percent, hitting $953 million in 1996 and have more than tripled in the past two years.
Poultry exports to China jumped nearly 76 percent in 1996 rising to $55 million from $32 million in 1995, USDA said.
